Latin word

missus

missus, missūs m.

noun, fourth declension

course; a heat, a round (of races or games)

In this lexicon

  • course

    also used · post-classical · M-O; Hist. Aug.

  • round

    the recommended word · classical · Suet. Dom. 4.3: centum missūs; Suet. Ner. 22: multiplicātīs missibus (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. inning, heat, round; Traupman 45; Traupman 333

Examples

  • circēnsium diē, quō facilius centum missūs peragerentur, singulōs ē septēnīs spatiīs ad quīna corripuit

    on the day of the circus games, so that a hundred races could be got through more easily, he cut each from seven laps to fiveSuet. Dom. 4.3

    In the entry for round

  • quīnque diērum spatiō fīniēbātur imperium ac per omnēs in orbem ībat

    each held power for five days, and it went round them all in turnLiv. 1.17.6

    In the entry for round
